items.title: design(tenancy): decide where per-tenant connection strings live

labels.name: priority:parked
labels.description: Parked, blocked, speculative, or intentionally deferred

labels.name: type:api-decision
labels.description: Public API or contract decision required

items.body:
## Target package or domain

`Headless.MultiTenancy` (where per-tenant infrastructure config would be modeled) and `Headless.EntityFramework` (where a resolved connection string would take effect).

## Problem statement

The tenant catalog shipped in #838 covers tenant *identity* only. There is no supported path to per-tenant data isolation beyond the shared-schema, filtered-column model that `HeadlessDbContext` implements today via the global query filter and the tenant write guard.

That leaves two topologies unsupported:

- **Schema-per-tenant** — one database, one schema per tenant.
- **Database-per-tenant** — a distinct database, and therefore a distinct connection string, per tenant.

This is deferred work, not rejected work. The catalog design explicitly separated two kinds of "not now", and per-tenant connection strings landed on the softer side: deferred alongside HTTP identifier strategies (#252), distributed-cache and remote-HTTP stores, and multi-identifier custom domains. It was held apart from the genuinely out-of-scope items — tenant CRUD/management APIs, and using the catalog as a per-tenant configuration store. Topology support was queued, not ruled out.

This issue exists to be that queue. Sibling deferred items were tracked as real issues; this one was not, and an untracked deferral is indistinguishable from an abandoned one.

## Decision required

A connection string *is* per-tenant configuration, and the framework has already taken a documented position on where per-tenant configuration lives. From the XML docs on the shipped `TenantInfo` type (`src/Headless.MultiTenancy.Abstractions/TenantInfo.cs`):

> Per-tenant application configuration does not belong on this model or in `ExtraProperties`: it belongs in Settings/Features/Permissions keyed by `Id`. This model owns tenant identity, routing (`Identifier`), and lifecycle (`IsEnabled`) only.

So this cannot be implemented without first resolving where the value lives. That is the gating decision, and it is why this is an `api-decision` issue rather than a straight feature.

### Option A — a connection-string property on `TenantInfo`

The Finbuckle shape. Cheapest to implement and the most familiar to anyone arriving from that library.

Cost: it contradicts the doc comment quoted above on a shipped public type, and reopens a decision that was argued at length during the catalog design. That decision was grounded in a measured outcome rather than taste: a review of Finbuckle at v10.1.0 found its `TTenantInfo` generic had spread through roughly 40% of its source files. Headless deliberately kept the tenant model to `Id`, `Identifier`, `Name`, `IsEnabled`, and `ExtraProperties`, and kept the entire pipeline — store SPI, catalog service, resolution, ambient context, caching — non-generic. Putting infrastructure config on the identity model is the first step back toward the shape that was rejected.

### Option B — resolve from Settings, keyed by canonical tenant id

Consistent with the documented contract, and reuses machinery that already exists.

Cost: there is no EF-layer mechanism for it, and there is a **bootstrapping hazard that needs a real answer**. The connection string must be known when the `DbContext` is constructed (`OnConfiguring`), but the EF-backed Settings store is itself a `DbContext`. Resolving a tenant's connection string from Settings that may live in a tenant-scoped database is circular. Any Option B design has to state which store answers the bootstrap read and prove it cannot recurse.

### Option C — a dedicated per-tenant infrastructure SPI

A small read-only seam (for example `ITenantInfrastructureStore`) separate from both `TenantInfo` and Settings, owning connection/schema resolution only.

Keeps the identity model clean and dodges the Settings recursion, at the cost of a third per-tenant lookup surface to configure, cache, and document.

## Design constraints to carry into whichever option wins

- **Connection pooling is the exhausted resource.** ADO.NET pools are keyed by connection string, so database-per-tenant multiplies pools rather than sharing one. On PostgreSQL the default `max_connections` of ~100 becomes the binding limit well before tenant count does. This is the strongest argument for treating schema-per-tenant as the default middle ground and database-per-tenant as the opt-in extreme.
- **Migrations need an out-of-DI path.** Applying migrations across tenants means constructing a context per tenant outside request scope. Finbuckle solves this with `MultiTenantDbContext.Create`; Headless needs an equivalent story, and it has to work with the design-time factory pattern the repo already uses.
- **Resolution timing.** The connection string has to be resolved after tenant resolution but before context construction. Registration-time `AddDbContext` configuration is too early.
- **Failure semantics must match the catalog's existing rules.** The catalog already fixes these: store faults propagate unwrapped as ordinary server errors, cache faults degrade to a miss that falls through to the store, and `OperationCanceledException` from the request token always propagates rather than triggering a store fallback. An infrastructure lookup on the request path must not invent different ones.
- **The tenant write guard and query filter stay as they are.** They key on canonical tenant id and are orthogonal to physical placement. A tenant in its own database still passes through them.
- **No guarantee exists in the shipped schema.** The v1 EF catalog schema was deliberately shaped so it would not preclude a future identifiers table. That forethought was applied to multi-identifier support only; nothing equivalent was done for connection or schema placement, so the storage layer carries no head start here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision between Option A, B, and C is recorded with its rationale, and `TenantInfo`'s XML doc contract is either upheld or explicitly amended.
- [ ] Shared-schema behavior is unchanged and requires no new configuration. Apps not opting in see no difference.
- [ ] Schema-per-tenant is supported, with the resolved schema applied to the model and to migrations.
- [ ] Database-per-tenant is supported, with the connection string resolved per tenant after tenant resolution.
- [ ] Connection-pool behavior under database-per-tenant is documented, including the `max_connections` ceiling and guidance on when schema-per-tenant is the better choice.
- [ ] Migrations can be applied across all tenants from outside DI, covered by an integration test against a real container.
- [ ] Infrastructure-lookup failure semantics match the catalog rules stated above.
- [ ] A tenant resolved to a non-default database or schema still has the query filter and write guard applied, covered by tests.
- [ ] `docs/llms/multi-tenancy.md` states which topologies are supported. It currently commits to logical isolation with a shared schema as the model, and that statement has to change with this work.

## Context

- Builds on the tenant catalog delivered in #838 (which closed #253).
- Related: #252 — HTTP identifier strategies, the sibling deferred item that was tracked.
- Prior art: Finbuckle.MultiTenant supports shared, separate, and hybrid topologies via a connection-string property on `TenantInfo`, switched after tenant resolution, with a `Defaults` section that individual tenants override. Consumers either implement `IMultiTenantDbContext` or derive from `MultiTenantDbContext`, and set the connection string in `OnConfiguring` rather than at `AddDbContext` registration. Its own tracker (Finbuckle issue #378) raises the per-database connection-pool problem noted above.

items.title: 🔍 Deep Repository Review: 5 Critical, 7 High, 18 Medium findings
items.body: # 🔍 Deep Review: microsoft/multiclouddb-sdk-for-java-samples **Date:** 2026-04-27 **Repo:** https://github.com/microsoft/multiclouddb-sdk-for-java-samples **Reviewer:** Copilot deep-review pipeline (3 parallel agents) --- ## 📊 Aggregate Finding Counts | Severity | TODO App | Risk Platform | Security | Total | |---|---|---|---|---| | 🔴 CRITICAL | 3 | 2 | 0 | **5** | | 🟠 HIGH | 3 | 4 | 0 | **7** | | 🟡 MEDIUM | 8 | 5 | 5 | **18** | | 🟢 LOW | 7 | 3 | 5 | **15** | | **Total** | **21** | **14** | **10** | **45** | --- ## 🚨 CRITICAL Findings ### C1. TodoApp: No client shutdown — resource leak **File:** `TodoApp.java` The `MulticloudDbClient` is created but never closed. No shutdown hook exists. Underlying Cosmos/Dynamo/Spanner connections leak on Ctrl+C. **Fix:** Add `Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook()` that calls `client.close()`. ### C2. TodoApp: No request body size limit — DoS **File:** `TodoApp.java` `MAPPER.readTree(exchange.getRequestBody())` reads entire stream with no size cap. Attacker can OOM the JVM. **Fix:** Add body length check before parsing. ### C3. TodoApp: Path traversal in static file handler **File:** `TodoApp.java` — `handleStatic()` URL path passed directly to `getResourceAsStream()`. Request like `GET /static/../logback.xml` could serve arbitrary classpath resources. `getResourceAsStream` does NOT normalize `..` segments. **Fix:** Normalize path, reject `..` segments, whitelist extensions. ### C4. Risk Platform: No Authentication or Authorization **File:** `RiskPlatformApp.java` Entire REST API is unauthenticated. Any client can read/write any tenant's data via `?tenant=`. Zero auth, zero tenant ownership checks. Developers copying this pattern into production would have a critical vulnerability. **Fix:** Add prominent WARNING in code/README about missing auth. ### C5. Risk Platform: XSS in Dashboard HTML **File:** `index.html` (riskplatform) User data rendered via template literals into `innerHTML` without sanitization. Portfolio name, alert message, symbol all injected raw. A portfolio named `` executes JS. **Fix:** Use `textContent` or sanitize helper before `innerHTML` insertion. --- ## 🟠 HIGH Findings ### H1. TodoApp: XSS via onclick handlers in index.html `escHtml()` escapes `<>&"` but NOT single quotes. IDs inside single-quoted JS `onclick` attrs can break out. Stored XSS risk. ### H2. TodoApp: CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` Wildcarding all origins on data-mutating API. Should warn this is not production-safe. ### H3. TodoApp: ConfigLoader silently swallows IOException If config file is malformed, returns empty config silently. Only treat null stream as optional. ### H4. Risk Platform: deletePosition Missing portfolio Query Param Client JS sends `DELETE /api/positions/{id}?tenant=X` but server requires `&portfolio=Y`. Every position delete returns 400. ### H5. Risk Platform: deleteAlert Missing portfolio Query Param Same bug as H4. Every alert delete returns 400. ### H6. Risk Platform: N+1 Query Pattern in Portfolio Listing For N portfolios, executes N+1 queries (1 list + N position lookups). Causes latency and RU cost at scale. ### H7. Risk Platform: Dashboard Fires 5+ Serial Queries 5 serial DB queries per dashboard load. No parallelism, no caching. --- ## 🟡 MEDIUM Findings (18 total) ### TODO App (8) - **M1:** Duplicates `ConfigLoader` logic instead of reusing it - **M2:** Spanner config has inconsistent database naming (`testdb` vs `todoapp`) - **M3:** `listTodos()` fetches only first page, no pagination - **M4:** `PortableCrudQuerySample` pagination demo is incomplete (prints `hasMore` but never fetches next page) - **M5:** Error responses leak internal exception messages and SDK categories - **M6:** `pom.xml` URL points to personal fork (`allenkim0129`) not microsoft org - **M7:** Cleanup scripts reference Risk Platform databases, no TODO app cleanup exists - **M8:** `HttpExchange` not always closed on error paths ### Risk Platform (5) - **M9:** No pagination — all queries read only first page (200 items max) - **M10:** Hardcoded tenant database names in `ResourceProvisioner` — no dynamic onboarding - **M11:** Query parameters not URL-decoded - **M12:** Cosmos emulator key in properties should have comment explaining it is well-known - **M13:** CORS allows all origins ### Security Cross-Cutting (5) - **M14:** HTTP servers bind to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) not `localhost` - **M15:** CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on both apps - **M16:** No request body size limits — `readAllBytes()` with no cap - **M17:** Error messages expose internal SDK details - **M18:** `MulticloudDbException` category leaked to client responses --- ## 🟢 LOW Findings (15 total, selected) - No `Content-Security-Policy` header on HTML pages - TodoApp `server.setExecutor(null)` uses single-thread executor - No input validation on document IDs (length, characters) - No rate limiting on either HTTP server - No authentication (expected for demo) - Naive query parameter parsing without URL decoding - Accessibility gaps in TODO UI (no ARIA roles, no screen reader support) - Inconsistent system property names (`todo.config` vs `multiclouddb.config`) - Risk Platform main file at 32KB/600 lines (acceptable for sample) - Dead code: unused `pad()` method in `RiskPlatformApp` --- ## ✅ What's Done Well | Area | Assessment | |---|---| | Credential Management | Emulator-only keys committed; cloud values gitignored with `.template` files | | SDK Usage | Correct use of `MulticloudDbClient`, `Key`, `ResourceAddress`, `QueryRequest` | | Multi-Tenant Model | Database-per-tenant via `ResourceAddress` — strongest isolation | | Partition Key Design | Positions grouped by portfolio — optimal for access patterns | | Provider Portability | Same code runs on Cosmos, DynamoDB, Spanner via config swap | | Schema Provisioning | `provisionSchema()` correctly used for multi-DB setup | | Portable Queries | Good demonstration of expression DSL with parameters | | Capabilities API | Displayed in both TODO and Risk Platform dashboards | | Cleanup Scripts | Named targets, preview before delete, interactive confirmation | | Dependencies | All recent versions, no known critical CVEs | --- ## SDK Feature Demonstration Coverage | Feature | Demonstrated | Quality | |---|---|---| | CRUD (create/read/update/delete/upsert) | ✅ Yes | Good | | Portable query DSL with parameters | ✅ Yes | Good | | Native query escape hatch | ✅ Yes | Good | | `provisionSchema()` | ✅ Yes | Good | | Capabilities API | ✅ Yes | Good | | `ResourceAddress` per-tenant routing | ✅ Yes | Excellent | | `QueryRequest.partitionKey()` scoping | ✅ Yes | Good | | Provider switching via config | ✅ Yes | Excellent | | Pagination with continuation tokens | ❌ No | Printed but never followed | | Error handling (category-specific) | ⚠️ Partial | Caught but not branched on | | Retry/backoff patterns | ❌ No | Not demonstrated | | Batch operations | ❌ No | Not demonstrated | | TTL / metadata | ❌ No | Not demonstrated | | ORDER BY / limit | ❌ No | Not demonstrated | --- ## 🎯 Top Priority Actions | # | Action | |---|---| | 1 | Fix path traversal in TodoApp static handler | | 2 | Fix XSS in both dashboards — sanitize user data | | 3 | Add shutdown hook to close `MulticloudDbClient` | | 4 | Fix broken delete buttons in Risk Platform (add `&portfolio=` param) | | 5 | Add request body size limits to both servers |

items.body:
## Current agreed context — 2026-10-07

**Scope:** Resolve declared dependencies/capabilities/versions into a consistent immutable bundle; core cannot be disabled and optional packs cannot be assumed.

**Required proof:** Check API/worker interpretation agreement and tenant-specific Spanner handshake before admission; no combination-specific dispatch or silent routing fallback.

**Shared decisions:** Core is mandatory. Optional memory/user/domain capabilities compose through declared dependencies, without pairwise hardcoded flows. Authenticated tenant identity resolves its authorized Spanner database and pack bundle; processing and retrieval use that same context. Never infer authorization from agent_id, caller-chosen database or artifact IDs.

**Tracking and status:** Parent #34 holds the reconciled six-bucket scope; #35/#42 own composition/capability controls, #43 tenant routing, #39 exact conformance and #41 real-Spanner execution. This is a scope/context reconciliation, not a fresh runtime verification. The issue remains open; historical reproductions below retain their original revision, backend and run scope. Historical memory probes are diagnostic evidence, not cloud acceptance. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration are required. Pinned documentation links below are historical published snapshots; newer local reports/run artifacts remain unpublished unless explicitly linked to a published revision.

---

A pack loading successfully does not establish that its required behavior is supported or that API and workers interpret accepted events consistently.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Define a small versioned capability/activation contract in existing pack/registry structures; refuse unsupported required behavior and expose optional inactive behavior.
- [ ] Define event owner versus permitted subscribers/dependencies, namespace collisions and unloaded-owner refusal, with explicit legacy exceptions.
- [ ] Choose persisted contract/binding/bundle metadata, available immutable historical interpreter artifacts and required consumer/profile obligations.
- [ ] Before new metadata is accepted, prove supported N/N−1 compatibility or controlled refusal/defer across API and applicable workers; digest alone is not an interpreter.
- [ ] Verify subscriber changes, required provider disabled and legacy readers. No live hot-reload framework is required.

Dependencies: coordinate #4/#5; metadata preservation prerequisite #27, lifecycle prerequisite #26 where applicable. Full historical repair/rebuild remains #11/#12/#13/#21. Slice1 policy; slice2 rollout gate.

Review findings: PE-05 / PE-06.

Parent feature: #34. Astra medium review references: docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md. Master plan: docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md (published documentation; see permanent links below). Reuse existing architecture; record policy decisions before affected runtime work. New requirements are not implemented or tested by this issue creation. Real acceptance uses tracked Engram→Spanner runs, not Redis/Neo4j runners or memory substitution. Local deterministic checks must be labeled separately.


## Published implementation context

- [This issue’s slice, scope and review gates](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pack-integration-context.md#issue-35) — slices **1;2;6**.

- [Astra medium review and conformance requirements](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md).
- [PDLC event contracts inventory](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv), [payload experiment matrix](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv), and [public-source corpus and remaining gaps](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md).

# Referral Queue Management Backend

*This specification defines the backend implementation of the student referral database model, status transitions, and coordinator/psychologist APIs, which is paired with the frontend specification in [todo/0007-referral-queue-management-frontend.md](0007-referral-queue-management-frontend.md).*

## Problem
Currently, there is no standardized, secure, or audited pipeline within App A.M.P.A.R.A. to escalate students showing critical psychological distress to specialized care. When teachers (Docentes) observe alarming behavioral or emotional patterns in students, they must communicate with the school's Pedagogical Coordinator (Coordenador Pedagógico) or mental health staff (psychologists/social workers) using unstructured channels like papers or text messages. This lacks accountability, leads to delayed or missed care for students in crisis, and violates Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD - Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados) by transmitting sensitive student health data without rigorous access logging and access control.

## Business Vision and Purposes
To ensure timely, coordinated, and compliant psychosocial intervention, the backend must support a robust, automated Referral Queue system. This feature enables pedagogical coordinators to act as secure gatekeepers who can centralize, prioritize, and assign student cases to specific mental health professionals. By tracking referral status from triage to resolution, the school maintains an audited, secure, and privacy-compliant ledger of care, ensuring no vulnerable student is left unassisted while strictly protecting sensitive data.

## Solution
We will implement an `Encaminhamento` (Referral) database model with isolated tables per tenant database and expose restricted APIs for case triage and assignment.
- A referral starts with a status of `"Aguardando Triagem"` (Pending Triage) and a default priority of `"Média"`.
- The Pedagogical Coordinator can list the full queue, set a custom priority (`"Baixa"`, `"Média"`, or `"Alta"`), add private coordinator observations, and assign the student to a specific registered psychologist or social worker.
- Once assigned, the referral's status can transition to `"Em Atendimento"` (Active Care) and ultimately `"Concluído"` (Resolved) or `"Arquivado"` (Archived), tracked via strict role-based access control.

## User Stories
1. As a Docente, I want to submit a formal referral request for a student under my care, describing their behavioral concerns, so that the coordinator can route them to support.
2. As a Coordenador Pedagógico, I want to list all referrals in my school, filtering them by priority and status, so that I can manage my team's workload and quickly identify students in critical need.
3. As a Coordenador Pedagógico, I want to update a referral's priority and assign it to a specific psychologist or social worker, so that they can take immediate action.
4. As an Equipe Multidisciplinar professional (psychologist/social worker), I want to view all referrals assigned specifically to me and transition their status as I provide care, so that I can document the progression of their treatment securely.

## Implementation Decisions

### Tenant-Level Database Models
We will add a new `Encaminhamento` model in `src/models.py` inside each school's tenant database:
1. `Encaminhamento` model:
   - `id` (INTEGER, primary key)
   - `estudante_id` (INTEGER, foreign key referencing `estudante(id)`, nullable=False)
   - `solicitante_id` (INTEGER, foreign key referencing `usuarios(id)`, nullable=False) - The teacher or coordinator who created the referral
   - `designado_id` (INTEGER, foreign key referencing `usuarios(id)`, nullable=True) - The psychologist or social worker assigned to the case
   - `motivo` (TEXT, nullable=False) - Verbatim description of behavioral or emotional distress
   - `observacoes_coordenacao` (TEXT, nullable=True) - Coordinator's private notes and internal logs
   - `prioridade` (VARCHAR(20), default='Média') - Values: `"Baixa"`, `"Média"`, `"Alta"`
   - `status` (VARCHAR(30), default='Aguardando Triagem') - Values: `"Aguardando Triagem"`, `"Em Atendimento"`, `"Concluído"`, `"Arquivado"`
   - `created_at` (TIMESTAMP)
   - `updated_at` (TIMESTAMP)

### State Machine Transition Rules
State transitions are strictly audited and guarded by Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):
- `"Aguardando Triagem"` -> `"Em Atendimento"`: Can be triggered only by the assigned `designado_id` (Psychologist/Social Worker) or the coordinator. Requires a non-null `designado_id`.
- `"Em Atendimento"` -> `"Concluído"`: Can be triggered only by the assigned `designado_id` or the coordinator. Represents a completed intervention.
- Any state -> `"Arquivado"`: Can be triggered only by the coordinator. Represents a case that was dismissed, resolved, or cancelled.

### API Endpoints and Contracts

#### 1. Submit a Referral
`POST /api/encaminhamentos`
- Description: Initiates a new student referral. Accessible to `docente` and `gestor_escolar` (coordinator) roles.
- Request Body:
```json
{
  "estudante_id": 25,
  "motivo": "Estudante tem se isolado frequentemente dos colegas e apresentou choro descontrolado na biblioteca durante o intervalo."
}
```
- Validations:
  - If `estudante_id` does not exist in the active tenant database, return status 404 Not Found with: `{"sucesso": false, "mensagem": "Estudante não encontrado."}`
- Actions:
  - Inserts a new row in the tenant's `encaminhamentos` table with `status="Aguardando Triagem"` and `prioridade="Média"`. Sets `solicitante_id` to the logged-in user.
- Response Status: 201 Created
- Response Body:
```json
{
  "sucesso": true,
  "mensagem": "Encaminhamento registrado com sucesso.",
  "id": 142
}
```

#### 2. List Referral Queue (Coordinator)
`GET /api/gestao/encaminhamentos`
- Description: Retrieves all student referrals inside the active tenant database. Accessible only to `gestor_escolar` / coordinator.
- Parameters: `status` (optional, string), `prioridade` (optional, string), `q` (optional, string - searches student name)
- Response Status: 200 OK
- Response Body:
```json
{
  "encaminhamentos": [
    {
      "id": 142,
      "estudante": {
        "id": 25,
        "nome": "Lucas Mendes de Oliveira",
        "matricula": "2026.01.0001",
        "turma": "1º Ano A"
      },
      "solicitante": {
        "id": 4,
        "nome": "Prof. Carlos Souza"
      },
      "designado": {
        "id": 8,
        "nome": "Psicóloga Amanda Costa"
      },
      "motivo": "Estudante tem se isolado frequentemente...",
      "prioridade": "Média",
      "status": "Aguardando Triagem",
      "created_at": "2026-09-12T10:15:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 3. Manage a Referral (Coordinator Triage)
`PUT /api/gestao/encaminhamentos/<int:id>`
- Description: Allows coordinators to triage a case by setting its priority, assigning it to a professional, or adding coordination notes.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Accessible only to coordinator)
- Request Body:
```json
{
  "prioridade": "Alta",
  "designado_id": 8,
  "observacoes_coordenacao": "Conversei com o professor e o caso requer atenção prioritária devido a recorrência de crises emocionais."
}
```
- Validations:
  - If the referral `id` does not exist, return 404.
  - If `designado_id` is provided but is not a user with the role `"equipe_multidisciplinar"`, return status 400 Bad Request with: `{"sucesso": false, "mensagem": "O profissional designado deve pertencer à equipe multidisciplinar."}`
- Actions:
  - Updates `prioridade`, `designado_id`, and `observacoes_coordenacao`. Updates `updated_at`.
- Response Status: 200 OK
- Response Body:
```json
{
  "sucesso": true,
  "mensagem": "Encaminhamento atualizado e designado com sucesso."
}
```

#### 4. List Assigned Referrals (Psychologist/Social Worker)
`GET /api/multidisciplinar/encaminhamentos`
- Description: Lists all referrals assigned to the currently logged-in professional. Accessible only to `"equipe_multidisciplinar"`.
- Parameters: `status` (optional, string)
- Response Status: 200 OK
- Response Body:
```json
{
  "encaminhamentos": [
    {
      "id": 142,
      "estudante": {
        "nome": "Lucas Mendes de Oliveira",
        "turma": "1º Ano A"
      },
      "motivo": "Estudante tem se isolado frequentemente...",
      "prioridade": "Alta",
      "status": "Aguardando Triagem",
      "created_at": "2026-09-12T10:15:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 5. Update Care Status (Psychologist/Social Worker)
`PUT /api/multidisciplinar/encaminhamentos/<int:id>/status`
- Description: Allows assigned professionals to transition the status of their cases as they deliver care.
- Request Body:
```json
{
  "status": "Em Atendimento"
}
```
- Validations:
  - The logged-in user must be the `designado_id` of the referral or the coordinator; otherwise, return status 403 Forbidden with: `{"sucesso": false, "mensagem": "Você não tem permissão para alterar o status deste caso."}`
  - The requested state must follow the State Machine Transition Rules (e.g., cannot move a concluded case back to awaiting triage).
- Response Status: 200 OK
- Response Body:
```json
{
  "sucesso": true,
  "mensagem": "Status do atendimento atualizado para 'Em Atendimento'."
}
```

## Testing Decisions
We will write exhaustive unit and behavioral tests under `backend/test/`:
- `test/test_models_encaminhamento.py`: Tests the `Encaminhamento` model constraints, foreign keys, and default values.
- `test/test_api_encaminhamentos_gestao.py`: Tests coordinator-only endpoints (`GET /api/gestao/encaminhamentos` and `PUT /api/gestao/encaminhamentos/<id>`), checking state validations, profile checks, and assigning invalid user roles (which must be blocked).
- `test/test_api_encaminhamentos_docente.py`: Tests the creation of referrals by teachers and blocks them from triaging or viewing other teachers' referrals.
- `test/test_api_encaminhamentos_multidisciplinar.py`: Tests psychologist-specific list and status transitions, verifying that a psychologist cannot transition or modify referrals assigned to other colleagues.

## Out of Scope
- Frontend dashboard screens, management tables, filters, and assignment modals (fully covered in [todo/0007-referral-queue-management-frontend.md](todo/0007-referral-queue-management-frontend.md)).
- Creation of electronic medical/psychological records (PEP). The system only tracks the state of the referral pipeline, not clinical session notes, protecting student medical privacy.
- External SMS/email notifications to parents or health clinics.

## Further Notes
The routing uses the same `database_router.py` database connection context to ensure that all query transactions and audits occur inside the isolated school database.

items.body:
## Situation

Row-level security (#26) on a shared schema is the right default, and it will not close every enterprise deal. Large hospital groups and government-linked institutions routinely require physical separation of their data as a procurement condition — their information-security questionnaire asks whether their records sit in the same tables as another organisation's, and "yes, but with policies" fails the question regardless of how sound the policies are. The architecture brief accordingly names schema-per-tenant and database-per-tenant as premium tiers.

Nothing supports this today. The data-access layer resolves one connection pool to one database with one `public` schema. If a tenant needed a separate schema or a separate database, there is no catalogue to look it up in, no routing to reach it, no way to run a migration across a variable set of targets, and no way for a NATS consumer or Temporal activity to reach the right database for the tenant on the message.

Affected: the enterprise sales motion, which currently has no answer to the separation question; the platform operations team, who would otherwise face manually managed one-off databases with divergent schema versions; the hospital admin at a separated tenant, who must see identical product behaviour; and the DPO, since data residency is a hard boundary and physical separation interacts directly with residency commitments.

This issue builds the isolation-mode framework — catalogue, routing, migration orchestration and observability — so that a tenant's storage topology becomes a configurable property rather than a fork of the platform. Issue #28 then productises the strongest mode as a commercial tier.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform engineer and as any product module
**I want** a tenant's storage topology — shared schema, dedicated schema, or dedicated database — to be a property resolved from a catalogue and applied transparently by the data-access layer
**So that** the same application code serves every tenant regardless of isolation mode, and schema changes reach every target reliably.

### Scope

**In scope**

* An `isolation_mode` property per tenant: `shared_schema`, `dedicated_schema`, `dedicated_database`, held in a control-plane tenant catalogue that is itself never tenant-partitioned.
* A connection resolver: given tenant context (#25), return the correct pool and, for `dedicated_schema`, set the `search_path` for the transaction alongside `app.tenant_id`.
* Bounded per-tenant pooling with a shared-pool fallback, so a hundred dedicated tenants do not exhaust database connections; pools are lazily created, idle-evicted and capped.
* Migration orchestration: a single logical migration version applied across all targets — the shared database, every dedicated schema and every dedicated database — as a Temporal workflow with per-target status, retry and resumability, plus a hard gate preventing application deploys when any target lags the required version.
* Schema-version reporting: an operational view showing every target's applied version and drift.
* RLS retained in every mode. A dedicated schema or database still carries `tenant_id` and its policies; separation is defence in depth, not a replacement.
* Event consumers and Temporal activities resolve the target from the same catalogue, so no execution path assumes the shared pool.
* Health, latency and connection metrics tagged by isolation mode and target.

**Out of scope**

* The commercial dedicated-database tier, entitlement and provisioning of new clusters — issue #28, which consumes this framework.
* Migrating an existing shared tenant's data into a separated target — issue #28 owns the cutover workflow.
* Country-level residency routing and regional deployments — the Country Profile epic; residency selects the region, this issue selects the target within it.
* Per-tenant encryption keys and isolated backups — the Data Isolation encryption and backup stories.
* Read-replica routing and analytics offload — the OLAP separation story.

---

## Recommended Solution

Introduce a control-plane catalogue and make the connection resolver the only component that knows about topology.

```sql
-- control plane; not tenant-partitioned, platform role only
CREATE TABLE tenant_storage (
  tenant_id      uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  isolation_mode text NOT NULL
      CHECK (isolation_mode IN ('shared_schema','dedicated_schema','dedicated_database')),
  region         text NOT NULL,                  -- residency boundary
  cluster_ref    text NOT NULL,                  -- CloudNativePG cluster name
  database_name  text NOT NULL,
  schema_name    text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'public',
  schema_version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status         text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', -- provisioning|active|migrating|readonly|retired
  secret_ref     text NOT NULL,                  -- vault path for credentials
  updated_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT schema_matches_mode CHECK (
    (isolation_mode = 'dedicated_schema') = (schema_name <> 'public')
    OR isolation_mode = 'dedicated_database')
);
```

Credentials are never stored here — only a vault reference, consistent with the secrets rule.

The resolver sits underneath the `Do` provider from #25, so callers are unchanged:

```go
func (p *Provider) Do(ctx context.Context, fn func(*gorm.DB) error) error {
    tc, err := FromContext(ctx); if err != nil { return ErrNoTenantContext }
    tgt, err := p.catalogue.Resolve(ctx, tc.TenantID)   // Redis-cached, NATS-invalidated
    if err != nil { return err }
    if tgt.Status == StatusMigrating { return ErrTenantReadOnly }
    db, err := p.pools.Get(tgt)                          // bounded, lazily created
    if err != nil { return err }
    return db.WithContext(ctx).Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error {
        if err := tx.Exec("SET LOCAL search_path = ?", tgt.SchemaName).Error; err != nil { return err }
        if err := tx.Exec("SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = ?", tc.TenantID).Error; err != nil { return err }
        return fn(tx)
    })
}
```

`search_path` is set with `SET LOCAL` for the same reason as `app.tenant_id` — a pooled connection must not carry it beyond the transaction. Setting both in one place means no module can get one without the other.

Pool management is the main operational risk. Each dedicated database gets a small pool (default 5, configurable per tenant through #23); pools are created on first use, evicted after 15 minutes idle, and the total across all pools is capped with a metric and alert at 80% of the cap. Dedicated *schemas* share the underlying cluster pool and cost nothing extra in connections, which is why `dedicated_schema` is the recommended middle tier.

Migration orchestration runs as a Temporal workflow, `SchemaMigrationWorkflow`, because it is long-running, must survive worker restarts and needs per-target retry:

```
MigrateAll(version) →
  fan out over tenant_storage targets (bounded parallelism, default 8)
    → per target: advisory lock, apply migration, update schema_version, emit progress
  → on any target failure: continue others, mark target degraded, do not roll back succeeded targets
  → completion: assert all active targets at target version
```

Migrations must therefore be backward-compatible and additive within a release — expand/contract only — because targets are transiently at different versions. The deploy gate enforces this from the other side: the application refuses to start if `min(schema_version)` across active targets is below its required minimum.

API surface (platform-only):

```
GET  /internal/tenant-storage                      (catalogue, filterable by mode/status)
GET  /internal/tenant-storage/{tenant_id}
POST /internal/tenant-storage/{tenant_id}/mode     { isolation_mode }  -- registers intent; cutover is #28
GET  /internal/schema-migrations/status            (per-target version and drift)
POST /internal/schema-migrations/run               { version }
GET  /internal/tenant-storage/pools                (pool utilisation by target)
```

Events:

```json
// platform.tenant_storage.changed
{ "tenant_id":"…", "isolation_mode":"dedicated_schema",
  "cluster_ref":"hms-in-prod-2", "schema_name":"t_9f2a", "status":"active" }
// platform.schema_migration.target_completed
{ "target":"hms-in-prod-2/hms/t_9f2a", "version":184, "duration_ms":9120 }
```

`platform.tenant_storage.changed` invalidates the resolver cache across every pod and every consumer, so routing converges without a restart.

OpenFGA — the catalogue is platform infrastructure and no tenant user may read it:

```
type tenant_storage
  relations
    define platform_operator: [user, service#member]
    define can_read: platform_operator
    define can_change_mode: [user, role#assignee] and platform_operator
```

Sequencing: depends on #25 (context and provider) and #26 (RLS, which stays on in all modes). Blocks #28. The Country Profile epic must define `region` semantics before dedicated targets are provisioned outside India.

Risks: (a) connection exhaustion as dedicated tenants grow — mitigated by bounded, idle-evicted pools, the utilisation alert, and steering most customers to `dedicated_schema`; (b) schema drift leaving one hospital on an old version — mitigated by the drift view, the deploy gate and an alert on any active target more than one version behind; (c) a resolver cache serving a stale target during a mode change — mitigated by `status = migrating` forcing read-only and by NATS invalidation on every catalogue change.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** three tenants configured as `shared_schema`, `dedicated_schema` and `dedicated_database` in the same region
**When** the identical application code path serves an equivalent request for each
**Then** each request is routed to its correct cluster, database and schema, `app.tenant_id` and `search_path` are both set within the transaction, results are identical in shape, RLS remains active in all three modes, and traces carry `isolation_mode` and `cluster_ref` attributes.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a tenant whose dedicated database cluster is unreachable — pod eviction or network partition
**When** a request for that tenant arrives
**Then** the resolver fails after a bounded connection timeout, the request returns `503` with a retry hint, no request is silently routed to the shared database, other tenants are entirely unaffected, and a `tenant_target_unavailable` alert fires identifying the cluster and tenant.

### Edge Cases

* A schema migration where one dedicated target fails mid-run — the workflow completes the remaining targets, marks the failed one degraded, is resumable from the failure point, and never leaves a partially applied migration on that target.
* Total pool count reaches the configured cap — new dedicated targets fail fast with a clear operational error and an alert, rather than starving existing pools of connections.
* A tenant in `status = migrating` receives a write — rejected with `ErrTenantReadOnly` and a user-visible maintenance message; reads continue to be served.
* A NATS consumer receives an event for a dedicated-database tenant while its resolver cache is cold — the resolver loads from the catalogue on demand; the message is redelivered rather than dead-lettered if the target is temporarily unavailable.
* A dedicated schema name collides with an existing schema — generation uses a tenant-derived prefix with a uniqueness constraint at the catalogue level, and provisioning fails before any DDL runs.
* A tenant is retired — its target moves to `readonly` then `retired`; pools are closed, the catalogue row is retained for audit, and requests return `410` rather than routing to a deleted database.
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** a tenant's storage topology is a catalogue property; the same application code serves shared-schema, dedicated-schema and dedicated-database tenants with identical behaviour, and schema changes reach every target with visible per-target status.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** the enterprise separation requirement can be answered concretely, and operations gains a single view of schema version across all targets instead of managing one-off databases by hand.
* **Success metric or validation method:** routing overhead adds under 2 ms at p95 versus the shared path; a migration across 50 targets completes within 10 minutes with per-target status and zero partially applied targets; schema drift across active targets is zero at the end of every deploy, enforced by the deploy gate; the adversarial isolation suite from #26 passes unchanged in all three modes; pool utilisation stays below 70% of cap at projected 12-month tenant counts.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 60 days after the first non-shared tenant, tracking pool utilisation, `tenant_target_unavailable` events, migration workflow failures and per-target version drift.

---
## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — all six items.
**Reason:** this issue delivers a connection resolver, a control-plane catalogue, pool management and a Temporal migration workflow. Its only interfaces are platform-internal JSON endpoints consumed by operations tooling; no end-user surface is produced.
**Alternative validation:** equivalence of behaviour across isolation modes is validated by running the existing product E2E suites against a `dedicated_schema` and a `dedicated_database` tenant as well as a shared one, which is a stronger check than a UI review. The operational drift view is delivered as an endpoint and rendered by existing dashboards.
**Residual risk:** none for accessibility. Residual operational risk is connection exhaustion and schema drift, both covered by explicit metrics, caps and the deploy gate.
**Approved by:** Security and Platform lead.
